title: NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH HYPOTONIA, LANGUAGE DELAY, AND SKELETAL DEFECTS WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES

intro.text: This entry describes a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by hypotonia, language delay, and skeletal defects, with seizures in some patients (NEDHLSS); the causal gene and the reports defining it are not recalled here with enough confidence to be stated.

checks.claim: The neurodevelopmental disorder NEDHLSS is characterized by hypotonia, language delay, and skeletal defects.
checks.evidence_quote: Twelve of 14 individuals in this group are hypotonic
checks.explanation: The paper does not use the name NEDHLSS. Its summary of the disorder lists developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism, epilepsy, hypotonia and ataxia, not 'skeletal defects'. Hypotonia, language delay (13/14 non-truncating, 10/11 truncating) and orthopedic abnormalities (12/14 non-truncating) are each reported, but the paper does not frame those three as the disorder's defining triad.

checks.claim: Some patients with NEDHLSS have seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: Ten of 14 individuals in our cohort with non-truncating variants have epilepsy, with onset ranging from 2 months to 8 years.
checks.explanation: Seizures occur in some patients but not all: 10/14 with non-truncating variants and 1/11 with truncating variants.

paragraphs.text: Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia, language delay, and skeletal defects with or without seizures (NEDHLSS) is a disorder of early childhood onset. As the name indicates, its main features are global developmental delay with especially poor speech and language development, hypotonia, and skeletal abnormalities. Some affected individuals also have seizures.

checks.claim: NEDHLSS (neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia, language delay, and skeletal defects with or without seizures) has its onset in early childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: All 14 individuals with non-truncating variants have a history of developmental delays or intellectual disability.
checks.explanation: Onset in early childhood is implied by the developmental delays, the prenatal and neonatal findings, and seizure onset as early as 2 months. The paper never states the age of onset explicitly.

checks.claim: Global developmental delay is a main feature of NEDHLSS.
checks.evidence_quote: All 14 individuals with non-truncating variants have a history of developmental delays or intellectual disability.
checks.explanation: The paper describes developmental delay as a core feature.

checks.claim: Speech and language development is especially poor in NEDHLSS.
checks.evidence_quote: These individuals as a group appeared to have more selective developmental abnormalities involving expressive language; 10/11 individuals in this group had delayed expressive language
checks.explanation: Language is especially affected: 10/11 with truncating variants had expressive language delay, and nine of the patients with non-truncating variants are non-verbal.

checks.claim: Hypotonia is a main feature of NEDHLSS.
checks.evidence_quote: Twelve of 14 individuals in this group are hypotonic
checks.explanation: Hypotonia is listed among the main features of the disorder.

checks.claim: Skeletal abnormalities are a main feature of NEDHLSS.
checks.evidence_quote: Orthopedic abnormalities were common in individuals with non-truncating variants (n = 12/14).
checks.explanation: Orthopedic and skeletal abnormalities were common in this group, including clubfoot, hip dysplasia, kyphoscoliosis and syndactyly.

checks.claim: Some individuals with NEDHLSS have seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: Ten of 14 individuals in our cohort with non-truncating variants have epilepsy, with onset ranging from 2 months to 8 years.
checks.explanation: Seizures are present in a subset of patients.
